4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One detailed bug report with screenshots filed as a GitHub Issue on your partner's repo, the bug filed on YOUR repo fixed and signed off by the tester who found it, and ROLLER v2 pushed with a changelog on your portfolio site — all by Sunday night.
4th Period.workingNow: Reproducing the bug filed on your repo, finding the JavaScript file it lives in, and fixing it with Copilot.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can reproduce the bug in my Issue, find which JavaScript file causes it, and push a fix that passes my own test by the end of class, so my game works the way I designed it.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.17 — Systematically test and refine programs using a range of test cases.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely literary and informational texts and viewing multimedia to determine how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language.
agenda: Mini-lecture: reproduce → find the file → fix → verify (7 min)
I do: reproduce a bug and write its fix spec (8 min)
You do: reproduce, fix with Copilot, and push (25 min)
Exit Ticket: comment on your Issue — what you changed (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Tuesday you wrote a bug report detailed enough for someone else to use. Today you're on the other side: you read the Issue filed on YOUR repo, make the bug happen on purpose, track it to the right JavaScript file, and fix it. Tomorrow the tester who found it checks your fix and you ship v2.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your finished game, published and embedded on your Google Site by Sunday night — with your tester notes and observer notes filled in, 1 bug fixed in your own game, and 3 sentences on what you changed and why.
6th Period.workingNow: Reading the bug report about your game, making the bug happen, and fixing it with Perplexity.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can make the bug from my report happen on purpose and fix it with Perplexity, so that by the end of class my game does what it should.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.17 — Systematically test and refine programs using a range of test cases.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely literary and informational texts and viewing multimedia to determine how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language.
agenda: Mini-lesson: report → make it happen → fix → check (6 min)
I do: read a report, make the bug happen (5 min)
You do: make your bug happen, fix it with Perplexity (29 min)
Exit Ticket: Did your fix work? How do you know? (5 min)
6th Period.connections: This week you tested someone's game and watched someone test yours. Today you use those notes: first make the bug happen on purpose — if you can't make it happen, you can't prove you fixed it — then fix it. Tomorrow your tester checks it and your game goes live.
